title: Learning gain differences between ChatGPT and human tutor generated algebra hints
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether hints generated by ChatGPT can support algebra learning as effectively as human-authored hints already used in an adaptive tutoring system. The authors focus on two research questions: how often ChatGPT produces low-quality hints, and whether learning gains from ChatGPT-generated hints differ from those from human tutor hints.

The intervention was an A/B experiment in the Open Adaptive Tutor (OATutor). For each algebra problem, ChatGPT was prompted to produce a worked-solution-style hint, and the outputs were manually quality-checked before use. The comparison condition used pre-authored human tutor hints from OATutor. The study included two algebra lessons: Elementary Algebra and Intermediate Algebra.

Participants were 77 Mechanical Turk workers with at least a high school degree and master status, randomly assigned to either ChatGPT or human-hint conditions and to one of the two lessons. Each session included a pre-test, five-item acquisition phase, and post-test. The main finding was that both conditions showed positive learning gains, but statistically significant gains occurred only in the human-hint condition. Human-authored hints outperformed ChatGPT hints in both lessons, and about 30% of ChatGPT hints were rejected during quality checking because they contained incorrect answers or incorrect solution steps. The authors conclude that ChatGPT-generated algebra hints are not yet a drop-in replacement for human-authored tutoring content and still require human supervision.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small randomized head-to-head experiment with random assignment to hint condition and lesson, but it is conducted with Mechanical Turk adults rather than the intended middle-school population and has only 77 participants. It is stronger than correlational evidence, yet there are notable concerns about external validity and a pre-test imbalance in Intermediate Algebra.
impact_tier_rationale: The observed learning effects are modest and mixed: both conditions improved, but ChatGPT underperformed human hints and was not statistically significant within-condition. Given the small sample and lack of clear positive advantage for the LLM, the practical impact is unclear to modest at best.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT-generated worked-solution hints for algebra tutoring problems in Open Adaptive Tutor, compared head-to-head against human-authored tutor hints in elementary and intermediate algebra lessons.
Open Adaptive Tutor (OATutor) delivering algebra practice with pre-test, acquisition phase, post-test, and hint/scaffold support used as the experimental platform and human-hint baseline.

finding.finding_summary: Across 77 Mechanical Turk participants, both ChatGPT and human-hint conditions showed positive pre-post learning gains in algebra, but gains were statistically significant only for the human-hint condition. In Elementary Algebra, gain was 24.63% for control vs 11.14% for ChatGPT; in Intermediate Algebra, 23.65% vs 1.7%, with between-condition differences statistically significant at p=0.038 in both topic areas.
finding.measure: Pre-test to post-test algebra accuracy / learning gain on repeated-item tests

finding.finding_summary: The human-authored hint condition produced statistically significant learning gains in both algebra topics, whereas the ChatGPT condition did not. In Elementary Algebra, average gain was 24.63% with pre-test 59.68% and post-test 84.32%; in Intermediate Algebra, average gain was 23.65% with pre-test 50.94% and post-test 74.59%.
finding.measure: Pre-test to post-test algebra accuracy / learning gain on repeated-item tests
